prototype_note: a probe over the same three pools ran while the tool was written and produced the headline numbers, so B1-B6 are confirmatory; they are written as structural claims so that an edited tool cannot pass them by accident

declared_acceptance_before_the_receipt_r.B1: the union of the three machines has strictly more distinct behaviours than any single machine
declared_acceptance_before_the_receipt_r.B2: the union's minimal class for the user's goal is strictly smaller than the richest single machine's
declared_acceptance_before_the_receipt_r.B3: the union's minimal class for the user's goal is still greater than one
declared_acceptance_before_the_receipt_r.B4: the third machine removes fewer minimal statements than the second
declared_acceptance_before_the_receipt_r.B5: the residual is log2(class) questions of the user, and no run can pay one of them
declared_acceptance_before_the_receipt_r.B6: zero model calls, zero stored parameters, every run executed

definitions.behaviour: the bitmask of a statement over every executed run: two statements are the same knowledge when their masks are equal
definitions.class: the number of minimal statements carrying one behaviour; a conjunction of two is non-minimal when one conjunct alone already carries it
definitions.residual: the class of the user's goal on the union: statements no run of any of the three machines can tell apart

limits: the grammar is supplied and small (244 terms over these machines' literals); the ceiling is computed for it, not for goals in general
three CLI machines at depths 5/4/4; depth 6 is out of reach here and named, not simulated
the synthesis side of coding is untouched: this prices what an edit would be for, not an edit
log2(k) is a count of questions, not a dialogue: it says what must be asked, not how well
